title: Leave a Trace
content:
What problem does this solve?
A program that never shows anything is difficult to understand. print() gives it a way to leave evidence of what it did.

Basic syntax
  print(value)
  print(value1, value2)
  # this is a comment

What actually happens
When Python reaches a print() call, it converts each argument to text, joins them with spaces by default, writes that text to the console, then continues with the next line. Multiple print() calls run from top to bottom in order. An argument is a value you pass into print() inside the parentheses.

Text in quotes is a string — literal text Python should take as written. Comments start with #. Python ignores them entirely; they are notes for humans, not instructions for the computer.

When this is useful
Use print() whenever you need to observe a value, a status line, or a short log. Use comments to record why a line exists.
concepts: print() writes values to the console
Text in quotes is a string — a piece of text Python should take literally
Multiple print() calls execute from top to bottom
Multiple arguments to print are separated by spaces
Lines starting with # are comments and do not run

examples.title: Recovered record
examples.code:
print("EXPEDITION LOG 17")
print("Party registered:", 4)
print("Status: OVERDUE")
examples.explanation: Three print calls run in order. The middle call passes two arguments — a string and a number — and inserts a space between them.

examples.title: Notes for humans
examples.code:
# Last report received three days ago
print("Search authorized")
examples.explanation: The comment is skipped. Only Search authorized appears in the console.

common_mistakes: Forgetting quotes around text: print(Hello) looks for a variable named Hello
Expecting comments to change program behavior — they never do
Assuming print adds commas or other punctuation between arguments — it only adds spaces

exercises.title: Predict the log
exercises.prompt: What does the following program print? Type the exact output (no quotes around the whole answer).
hints: Read the program from top to bottom — each print becomes its own line.
print joins multiple arguments with a single space.
The first line is WAYSTATION 7; the second line is Expedition: then a space then 17.
exercises.failure_message: Check spacing, capitalization, and that each print ends up on its own line.

exercises.title: Fix the record
exercises.prompt:
This line is supposed to print exactly:
EXPEDITION 17

It is broken. Repair it so literal text is treated as a string.
hints: Python needs to know whether EXPEDITION 17 is a name or literal text.
Wrap the whole message in quotes: print("EXPEDITION 17").

exercises.title: Create the dispatch
exercises.prompt:
Write a short dispatch that prints exactly these three lines:
SEARCH DISPATCH
Expedition: 17
Status: OVERDUE

Requirements:
- use three print() calls
- include at least one real comment (a # note for humans)
- the Expedition line must use two arguments to print (the label and the number)
hints: Think about one print per line of output, plus a # comment somewhere.
For the Expedition line, pass a string and the number 17 as two separate arguments.
A working shape is: print("SEARCH DISPATCH"), then print("Expedition:", 17), then print("Status: OVERDUE"), with a # comment on its own line.

tests.message: Add a comment that starts with # and explains something about the dispatch.

exercises.success_message: Dispatch recorded. Your program left a readable trace of Expedition 17.
